To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified 2 truncating mutations and some variants in PALB2 gene in non-BRACA1/BRCA1 breast/ovarian families selected from either a family or personal history of pancreatic cancer.
we have identified two novel PALB2 truncation mutations, one of them a novel frameshift, in two families from a cohort of BRCA1 and BRCA2 negative breast/ovarian families with pancreatic cancer.
PALB2 mutations were identified in two families with breast/ovarian cancers selected from either a family or personal pancreatic cancer history.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of PALB2 as a potential candidate gene for pancreatic cancer.
identifying the genes responsible for hereditary breast and ovarian cancer, as well as the genes involved in hereditary breast and pancreatic cancer.
the identification of genes that predispose to breast/pancreas cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PALB2 gene does not appear to have a significant role in pancreatic cancer susceptibility.
the prevalence rate of PALD2 mutations in BRCA1 and BRCA2 negative families with pancreatic cancer is similar to that of unselected breast cancer families.
PALB2 mutations are not a frequent cause of hereditary breast/ovarian and pancreatic cancer in our Spanish population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PALB2 is not a common cause of hereditary breast cancer in our population.
the PALB2 gene is a good target for genetic testing of breast cancer patients with a family history of pancreatic carcinoma.
PALB2 gene should be included in the genetic testing of patients with familial breast/ovarian/pancreatic cancers, especially those with a personal or family breast/pancreas cancer history.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PALB2 mutations are not a common cause of breast cancer in families with pancreatic cancer.
the PALB2 gene is a good candidate for the development of breast cancer in families with a pancreatic cancer history.
PALB2 mutations are a rare cause of breast/ovarian and pancreatic cancer in Spanish families.
